x: Sale's Kevin McKay used the craft gained over years of international competition to get ahead of Tom Lerwill in the 'eight' but we were piling up the points steadily and with 'bankers Neil Owen, Kevin Brown, Leith Marar, Mike Edwards and Fred Salle all winning - and decathlete Simon Shirley plugging…

He had some large gaps to bridge but nevertheless, Birchfield, Morpeth, Liverpool and Sheffield were just some of the teams that fell to his all-devouring stride and he must have been delighted at out-running Sale's Kevin McKay by ten seconds.
So effective was he that he held off Olympics bound Kevin McKay for a fine win and a notable scalp. Matt Kloiber showed that he was over his illness problems with a solid 3rd spot in the 'B' race.

He finished just 3 seconds outside the medals as Sale's Kevin McKay grabbed 3rd in 36:49 to the Belgravian's 36:52. At Chigwell Tony Barden was 15th in the Essex Champs in 45:44 (winning time 42:00) while at Gillingham the Kent title was won in 38:18 by Medway's Royden with our own Phil Carstairs 18th in 42:15.
Jason Lobo doubled up on his first League appearance for us and finished a fine second in the 'A' 800m with a surprised Kevin McKay of Sale back in 5th spot.

Lee Hurst reduced the deficit in the 3000 s/c and Jason Lobo pulled back more points to finish a fine second in the 1500m to Kevin McKay. Birchfield then came to our aid in the shot with an unknown American outthrowing Newham Mark Proctor with Matt Simson third.

Left: Jason Lobo leads the Gold Cup 1500 metres mid-way through the race. He eventually placed 2nd to Kevin McKay (Sale) pictured here close up behind the Belgrave man. Jason finished the season with best 1998 performances of 49.6/ 1:47.48/3:48.90 for 400m through 1500m.
